response.rationale: All 10 evidence items are positive and none are negative, including T1 sources (a meta-analysis, Dunlosky 2013) and T4 sources (Chi 1989) showing that self-explanation, a form of elaboration, improves learning and problem-solving. Two caveats limit confidence. Several items repeat the same claim, and Dunlosky rates elaborative interrogation and self-explanation only "moderate" utility. The evidence also mostly shows that elaboration causes learning gains, which is a little different from "predicts achievement".
